description: Remediates CLAUDE-AUTH-009. Three execution layers now refuse to operate on a workspace that contains symlink(s): (1) source_mutation_rollback_snapshot.take_snapshot, (2) source_mutation_apply_after_approval.apply_after_approval, (3) source_mutation_rollback_execution.execute_rollback. The previous code paths called Path.is_file() (follows symlinks) and shutil.copytree(symlinks=False) (follows symlinks). A workspace containing a hostile symlink (e.g. pointing at /etc/passwd) would have had TARGET content snapshotted and then restored as a regular file at restore time. Rather than implement cross-platform symlink-target tracking (link semantics, link-of-link chains, non-existing targets), this lock takes the conservative path: refuse outright and ask the operator to resolve the workspace to a symlink-free state before retrying. The symlink check is implemented in scripts/repair/symlink_policy.py using Path.is_symlink() (does NOT follow links). Each layer surfaces a layer-specific token: ROLLBACK_SNAPSHOT_BLOCKED_SYMLINKS_UNSUPPORTED, SOURCE_MUTATION_BLOCKED_SYMLINKS_UNSUPPORTED, SOURCE_ROLLBACK_BLOCKED_SYMLINKS_UNSUPPORTED. Defense-in-depth: each layer checks its own invariants and never trusts upstream callers.
purpose: Rung 8 of the Claude authority leak remediation campaign.
host_note: Symlink-creation tests are skipped on hosts that lack the privilege to create symlinks (Windows without Developer Mode or SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege). The lock's defensive checks still execute; only the integration coverage that needs a real symlink in the workspace is skipped on those hosts.
